summary.en: Israel has intensified artillery shelling of southern Lebanese towns, including a reported strike on a town and an explosion in Bani Hayyan, while Israeli drones have followed a woman entering a home in south Lebanon. Hezbollah has responded with artillery fire on Israeli positions and has begun distributing its first cash payments to war victims and displaced families. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon due to the fighting. These aid payments and the drone surveillance of civilians are new developments compared with the earlier brief on airstrikes and displacement.
summary.nb: Israel har økt artilleriskyttingen mot sørlige libanesiske byer, inkludert et rapportert angrep på en by og en eksplosjon i Bani Hayyan, mens israelske droner har fulgt en kvinne som gikk inn i et hus i sør-Libanon. Hizbollah har svart med artilleriskudd mot israelske posisjoner og har begynt å dele ut sine første kontantutbetalinger til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. FN rapporterer at 300 000 personer er fordrevne i Libanon på grunn av kampene. Disse hjelpetilskuddene og dronovervåkingen av sivile er nye utviklinger sammenlignet med den tidligere oppsummeringen av luftangrep og fordrivelse.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
